iOS 27 beta 5 was released this week, confirming a feature Apple had previously hinted at: pay to upgrade to a higher-tier iCloud+ plan to unlock more Apple Intelligence features.

Upgrading your iCloud+ plan unlocks more iOS 27 AI features

If you're already subscribed to iCloud+ or Apple One, upgrading to iOS 27 will bring new features.

You'll get more Apple Intelligence features with usage limits (such as image generation), as well as new HomeKit secure recording features for your cameras.

But based on information from iOS 27 beta 5, the limits on these new features appear to depend on which iCloud+ plan you're subscribed to.

In the Home app → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence → Cameras & Language section, iOS 27 will now display how many cameras your iCloud+ plan supports for the AI summary feature. Quoting Stephen Robles' post on X:

The right-hand image shared by Robles shows that after tapping "View iCloud+ Plans" from the Cameras & Language page, a new screen appears with the following text:

Upgrade your iCloud+ plan to enjoy more Apple Intelligence features. Get more intelligent features, more storage, and more.

The page will display your current plan and offer options to upgrade to a higher tier. The page doesn't list all the different plans yet, which is very likely a minor beta issue that will be fixed before official release.

Based on what I've seen so far in the beta version, the 2TB iCloud+ plan appears to offer AI summaries for 5 cameras, while the 12TB plan supports up to 15. The details for other plans are not yet clear.

But based on the wording of this new upgrade page in the beta, it's almost certain that each higher tier of iCloud+ plan will not only support AI summaries for more cameras, but also increase the usage quotas for other AI features.

This is consistent with what CEO Tim Cook said on Apple's last earnings call.

What are your thoughts on Apple tying AI feature limits to iCloud+ plans? Feel free to leave a comment and let us know.
